note: THE RULE: in Emacs a `$' is an anchor only at the END of the regexp or before `\\|' or `\\)'; ANYWHERE ELSE IT IS A LITERAL DOLLAR. Emacs answers (0 nil 0): "a$b" matches the text "a$b" and does NOT match "ab", and "a$*" -- a dollar with a quantifier after it -- matches "a$$". kg answers (nil nil nil): its engine treats `$' as an anchor everywhere, so every one of these is a pattern that can never match. This is the seam under `s-lex-format'.
